bracket: [Textbook answer-key error: the book prints (16.17 mm Hg). Raoult's law gives \(P_1 = P_1^0x_1 = 17 \times 2.7778/(2.7778 + 0.04667) = 16.72\) mm Hg for 2.8 g of urea (60 \(\mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}\)) in 50 g of water, and the dilute-solution approximation gives 16.71 mm Hg — the same to three significant figures. The printed value would require about 8.6 g of urea, and appears to be 16.71 with its last two digits transposed.]

[Textbook misprint: the printed working sets a MINUS sign where a multiplication sign belongs, writing "2.315 g - 78 g/mol" in all three lines that carry the numerator. The operator has been corrected below, and the final unit, printed as "g mol", restored to \(\mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}\). The answer 58.96 \(\mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}\) is correct.]
